cards.title: Useful intelligence per watt
cards.summary: Huang frames inference around constrained power, token throughput and response speed.
cards.interpretation: If inference demand grows, system efficiency may matter as much as model capability. This is not a guaranteed market outcome.
cards.opportunity: Measure cost per successful task alongside latency and quality. Study inference serving.

cards.title: The agent opportunity is the feedback loop
cards.summary: Wang describes agents improving measurable outcomes through repeated feedback and coordination.
cards.interpretation: A workflow with measurable feedback may suit a bounded agent loop. Internal results do not establish workforce-replacement outcomes.
cards.opportunity: Pick one measurable workflow. Define success and failure, then compare a bounded loop against a baseline.

cards.title: Capability and adoption run on different clocks
cards.summary: Amodei distinguishes technical capability forecasts from uncertain economic adoption and compute-investment timing.
cards.interpretation: A model milestone alone is weak evidence for a revenue timeline. His capability timelines are forecasts.
cards.opportunity: Investigate procurement, integration, trust and workflow barriers before assuming benchmark gains create demand.

cards.title: Build an autonomy dial
cards.summary: Karpathy describes powerful but fallible LLMs and partially autonomous products that keep people in the loop.
cards.interpretation: A visible review loop may create dependable value. This is a design hypothesis to test, not a performance guarantee.
cards.opportunity: Prototype draft, review and execute modes. Measure review time and accepted results.

cards.title: Make the idea concrete before making it fast
cards.summary: Ng emphasizes concrete product ideas and human judgment as AI accelerates implementation.
cards.interpretation: Faster building increases the value of choosing and testing the right problem. No universal productivity multiplier follows.
cards.opportunity: Write a specific user, task and success criterion before prototyping. Combine implementation with customer discovery.

cards.title: The next interface may be the physical world
cards.summary: Li argues for intelligence that models the three-dimensional world, beyond language.
cards.interpretation: Spatial systems could create opportunities beyond chat. Reliability, timelines and commercial winners remain uncertain.
cards.opportunity: Explore vision, geometry and simulation. Test a narrow spatial task against real-world ground truth.

cards.title: A brilliant answer is not general intelligence
cards.summary: Hassabis emphasizes broad, consistent capability and novel discoveries when discussing his criteria for AGI.
cards.interpretation: A strong demonstration does not establish reliable performance across a whole workflow. Test gaps as well as highlights.
cards.opportunity: Build evaluations around failure modes, domain coverage and distribution shift.

cards.title: Compute is a system, not just a chip
cards.summary: Huang presented Blackwell alongside networking and rack-scale systems for larger AI workloads.
cards.interpretation: For builders, memory and communication can matter as much as nominal compute. Benchmark the entire serving path.
cards.opportunity: Measure latency, memory use and cost per successful task before changing hardware.

cards.title: Packaging models is product work
cards.summary: Huang introduced NIM microservices to package and deploy AI models through standard APIs.
cards.interpretation: Deployment interfaces can turn model capability into something a team can operate. The announcement alone proves no product fit.
cards.opportunity: Prototype one bounded workflow and compare integration effort with your current stack.

cards.title: Simulation is a practice ground
cards.summary: Huang described simulated environments for robot learning and introduced tools for perception and manipulation.
cards.interpretation: If simulation transfers reliably to physical tasks, it could shorten iteration. Real-world safety still needs direct validation.
cards.opportunity: Study sim-to-real failures and test one task in both environments.

cards.title: Better data deserves a seat at the table
cards.summary: Wang argued that high-quality datasets and efficient human feedback were bottlenecks as compute and models grew.
cards.interpretation: Treat dataset quality as engineering work. More data helps only when it addresses the failures you actually observe.
cards.opportunity: Build a small error taxonomy and show how targeted labels change held-out performance.

cards.title: A scaling forecast is still a forecast
cards.summary: Wang forecast growth in compute and data, with new model capabilities emerging from scale.
cards.interpretation: Scaling may improve capability, but a historical prediction does not guarantee every task improves or every business benefits.
cards.opportunity: Compare a smaller and larger model on the same representative evaluation set.

cards.title: Start with the workflow, then adapt the model
cards.summary: The keynote summary describes pretrained models and task-specific tuning as routes for enterprises without in-house model expertise.
cards.interpretation: A pretrained model can reduce the starting cost. Owning evaluation and domain context remains your team’s responsibility.
cards.opportunity: Choose one costly repeatable task; test the baseline before considering fine-tuning.

cards.title: Seeing should lead to acting
cards.summary: Li describes spatial intelligence as processing visual information, predicting outcomes and acting in the physical world.
cards.interpretation: If systems connect perception to reliable action, useful applications may extend beyond text. Reliability and human needs remain constraints.
cards.opportunity: Try a perception task with changing viewpoints and document where the system fails.
